key_insight: Directly optimizing pass@k balances candidate quality and diversity by selecting partial solutions to maximize the probability that at least one finishes correctly.
engineering_relevance: Pruning reasoning candidates after short prefixes can reduce inference computation while retaining a promising pool for continued generation.
method: Generate short prefixes for multiple candidate solutions.
Select a survivor pool by optimizing its probability of producing at least one correct completion.
Continue selected candidates, balancing quality and redundancy within one objective.
evidence_signal: Across eight open-weight reasoning models, the method outperforms quality-based and diversity-based pruning baselines, with especially pronounced gains when retaining a moderate number of candidates.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify how pool-level success probabilities are estimated or quantify pruning overhead, leaving deployment cost-effectiveness uncertain.
paper_title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
